findings.title: Revision matching delays one editor's delivery
findings.claim: One editor reports repeated manual revision matching and a late delivery. Another creator finds existing labels sufficient.

evidence.quote: I spend 60% of my own editing time checking which transcript revision matches the audio.
I copied three transcript versions into a spreadsheet yesterday and delivered the episode a day late.

counterevidence.quote: The free labels in my current editor are enough for my solo show. I would not pay for another app.

findings.counterevidence_search: All five invented records were inspected, including the sufficient-alternative case.
findings.uncertainty: Synthetic illustration only; no inference about real users or market prevalence.
findings.task: Match transcript revisions to an audio edit
findings.consequence: One speaker reports delivering an episode a day late.
findings.workaround: Manually copy versions into a spreadsheet.
findings.next_test: Ask editors to walk through their last revision handoff and compare existing labels against a checker prototype.

quantities.quote: I spend 60% of my own editing time checking which transcript revision matches the audio.
quantities.denominator_description: This editor's own editing time, not a share of people

dimensions.name: consequence
dimensions.rationale: One reported missed delivery; analyst-assigned severity.

dimensions.name: independent_support
dimensions.rationale: Two messages are from the same editor.

findings.title: A checker is a suggested solution
findings.claim: A viewer proposes a revision checker but explicitly says they have not used one. Adoption and usefulness are untested.

evidence.quote: You could build an automatic revision checker. I have never used one.

findings.counterevidence_search: All five invented records were inspected, including the sufficient-alternative case.
findings.uncertainty: Synthetic illustration only; no inference about real users or market prevalence.
findings.recommendation: Treat the proposed feature as a testable idea.
findings.next_test: Observe a real edit before choosing the solution.

dimensions.name: usefulness
dimensions.rationale: No observed use of a checker.

findings.title: The operator is not the payer
findings.claim: A studio operator reports an employer-funded subscription and states they neither choose nor pay for it.

evidence.quote: Our studio pays 18 dollars a month for the review app. I operate it, but I do not choose or pay for the subscription.

findings.counterevidence_search: All five invented records were inspected, including the sufficient-alternative case.
findings.uncertainty: Synthetic illustration only; no inference about real users or market prevalence.
findings.payer: The operator's studio, according to this speaker
findings.payment_evidence: Reported studio payment; no transaction independently verified.
findings.next_test: Interview whoever approves studio software purchases.
